newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices rise, eyes on bond-bund gap.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices rise, eyes on bond-bund gap.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose slightly on Tuesday on a market losing its EMU fears and focused on the Danish-German 10-year yield gap.

"The activity is in the spread trade between Germany and Denmark, I believe that the gap on the long bond will come down to 60 basis points in the course of the next few weeks," a dealer said, referring to the seven percent 2007 state bond.
By 1310 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 rose to 112.12, yielding 6.15 percent, from Monday's 111.91.
The seven percent 2007, due to become the benchmark on September 1, rose to 104.72, yielding 6.35 percent, from 104.39.

The 2006 bond's yield gap to the 10-year bund was unchanged at 45 basis points. The 2007 gap to the bund was likewise static at 65 b.p. Turnover in the 2006 was a thin 440 million crowns and in the 2007 just 100 million.

The benchmark's September future slipped 0.63 to 111.24, with 185 contracts traded and the six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.37 point to 90.40. The crown firmed slightly, to 3.8082 to the mark, from Monday's 3.8084.
Dealers said that the central bank sold in the six percent 2002, five percent 2005 and four percent 2000. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
